admission.justification: The named deadline turns a missing protocol answer into an ordinary failure the run continues past, instead of the asyncio wait that never returned in the combined run; the late-response case proves the failure fires.

applicability: The reader protocol exercise and its Git status observations, and the late-response regression beside them.
conditions: A passed limit is an ordinary assertion failure naming the responses that did not arrive.
exclusions: The limit's length is not part of the obligation; the late-response case deliberately shortens only its own response wait after session initialization.

evidence: notes/reports/role-launch/260928-MIK-L70-reviewer-6e032287-e04b-460f-82cf-fb4f25d0808a-fixverify-evidence/logs/V3-focused-touched-modules.txt (the late-response case passes); W-F2c-reader-deadline-removed.txt (with the limit removed the case does not pass)

statement: The reader protocol exercise runs under one 60-second limit and its Git status observations under a subprocess limit, and a passed limit is an ordinary assertion failure saying that the reader protocol responses did not arrive, after which the same process goes on to its next test.
